validated_work_order.understanding: All three follow-ups from #44 reproduce on main as filed, and all three are kept. (1) Review: the fixture guard in the new #44 test (test/web/pages.test.js, the 'seeded' assertion before the render loop) counts only lead_qualified events — the denominator. The spend.observed row that carries 3_000_000_000 micros is the numerator and is unguarded, so a fixture that stops carrying the amount still passes the guard and then fails at the CPL assertion with 'got —', which reads as a currency regression. Verified: the guard filters on event_type === 'lead_qualified' and asserts a count of 1. (2) Review: the same test re-creates the tenant_usd + opp_usd_expensive block and the seven-line `envelope` closure that already exist twice in the file. Verified on main: lines 931-941 and 978-988 are identical, and the `envelope` closure at 1001-1006 differs from the ones at 295-300 and 339-344 only in the tenant_id literal. freshRepos()/seededRepos() at the top are the file's established idiom for this. The reviewer's own note says the fence around the two existing USD tests belongs to whoever owns the order — that is this order, and it is lifted here deliberately. (3) QA: ISO_CURRENCIES.includes is exact, so a tenant row holding 'usd', 'Usd' or ' USD ' never resolves. I reproduced this against main and it is WORSE than the report says, so the 'minor' severity does not stand. For a 'usd' tenant the opportunity row renders 'value ₹6,000.00' as reported, but the Qualified CPL tile renders '—' and the dashboard insight spend renders '₹4,000.00'. The em-dash is not the money fallback: computeFunnel(rows, 'usd') excludes every spend row whose payload currency is 'USD', so the numerator is silently zero. GET /v1/metrics zeroes the same way, and POST /v1/events 400s CURRENCY_MISMATCH on a legitimate USD spend for such a tenant. A missing number on the primary objective (TR-9) is a different failure from a mislabelled one. The blast radius is still narrow and the trigger is external: measurement.js validates ingest currency against ISO_CURRENCIES exactly, and routes.js seeds a new tenant's currency from that validated code, so nothing the app itself writes today produces a non-canonical code. The bug is that the read path is not defensive about a row it did not write (a human UPDATE, a legacy import, a future write path).
validated_work_order.root_cause: One exact-match membership test standing in for currency identity, at every point where a stored tenant code is read. A code is stored as an arbitrary string (tenants.create takes any string; the column is TEXT), but three consumers compare it by exact string equality: money()'s ISO_CURRENCIES.includes guard in src/web/pages.js, computeFunnel's tenant-currency exclusion (src/domain/measurement.js:203), and routes.js:146's CURRENCY_MISMATCH check. 'usd' and 'USD' are the same unit of account, so all three treat the tenant's own spend as foreign and either relabel it or drop it. Nothing canonicalises between the row and those three comparisons.
validated_work_order.approach: Add one exported boundary function to the domain — canonicalCurrency(code) in src/domain/money.js, which trims and upper-cases a stored string and returns the ISO 4217 code it names, or null when it names none ('ZZZ' still resolves to null, so the documented bad-data INR fallback and the never-500 behaviour are unchanged). Then resolve every read of a tenant row's currency through it, in one seam per module, rather than touching the three comparisons individually: pages.js gets a local tenantCurrency(tenant) helper used at all six `tenant?.currency ?? 'INR'` sites, and money() itself canonicalises before the fallback so any value that reaches it renders in its own unit. routes.js gets a local helper used at both reads of the row — the mismatch check and the metrics filter — with the comparison canonicalising while the 400's message and details keep reporting the stored string verbatim, so every existing 400 is byte-identical and only the mis-cased tenant changes from rejected to accepted. Read-side only, deliberately: the QA repro sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE, which never touches tenants.create, so a write-side fix would not have fixed the reported case; and the existing test at test/web/pages.test.js:1077 pins tenants.create accepting any string, so tightening the write path would break a deliberate contract for no gain on the reported defect. Separately, close the two review findings in the same test file: lift the repeated tenant+opportunity block into a usdRepos() helper beside freshRepos() and the repeated envelope closure into one tenant-parameterised validatedEnvelope(), and have all three call sites use them; and extend the fixture guard to assert the resolved spend amount alongside the qualified-lead count, so a broken numerator fails at the guard with a fixture-shaped message instead of surfacing at the money assertion as an em-dash.

files.change: Export a new canonicalCurrency(currency): trims and upper-cases a stored code and returns the ISO_CURRENCI7 code it names, or null when it names none (non-string, empty/whitespace, or an unknown code like 'ZZZ'). Document why case and whitespace are not currency errors and why a genuinely unknown code is still a data error. Leave assertValidCurrency strict: fromMicros/fromMicros' contract stays 'a code I can render', and loosening it would change INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour test/domain/money.test.js already pins. The new function is the read-time boundary, not a second constructor.
files.why: One place decides what a stored code means. TR-1: a tenant's amounts carry a real ISO unit of account.

files.change: Import canonicalCurrency. Add a local helper that reads a tenant row and returns canonicalCurrency(row?.currency) ?? 'INR', and use it for the GET /v1/metrics tenantCurrency at the computeFunnel call. At the POST /v1/events CURRENCY_MISMATCH check, compare the canonical form of the stored row's code against the event's already-canonical spend currency, while the error's message and details keep reporting existingTenant.currency verbatim — so an unknown-code tenant ('ZZZ') still 400s with exactly today's message, and only a mis-cased or padded tenant code changes from rejected to accepted. Do not change the write of a new tenant row: the currency it is seeded with comes from a validated event code and is already canonical.
files.why: The same defect reaches the JSON surface twice: metrics zeroes the tenant's own spend, and ingest rejects a legitimate USD spend for a tenant whose row is merely mis-cased.

cases: canonicalCurrency resolves an already-canonical code to itself: 'USD' -> 'USD', 'INR' -> 'INR'
canonicalCurrency resolves a padded code: ' USD ' -> 'USD', '\nINR\t' -> 'INR'
canonicalCurrency returns null for a code that names no ISO currency: 'ZZZ' -> null
canonicalCurrency returns null without throwing for a non-string: undefined, null, 42, {}, and for '' and '   '

The regression this ticket exists to remove, on the shipped app. On main, step 4 reads 'value ₹6,000.00', the Qualified CPL tile reads '—', the insight spend reads '₹4,000.00', GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 0 with qualified_cpl_micros null, and POST of a USD spend.observed to that tenant is a 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH.

sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE tenants SET currency = 'usd' WHERE id = 'tenant_demo'" then reload /opportunities: [data-testid=opportunity-row] [data-component=value_micros] must read 'value $6,000.00' and the row must contain no rupee sign. Reload /: the meta-adSets section must contain '$500.00' and meta-insights '$4,000.00', and neither a '₹500.00' nor a '₹4,000.00' anywhere in the response.

On the same 'usd' tenant, the Qualified CPL kpi-card must read a number — '$3,000.00' against a seeded run — and must NOT read '—'. Then run the same two reads again with the currency set to ' USD ' and confirm they are byte-identical to the 'usd' run.

curl -s localhost:3100/v1/metrics?tenant_id=tenant_demo | jq '{spend_micros, qualified_volume, qualified_cpl_micros}' — spend_micros must be the seeded non-zero amount and qualified_cpl_micros must not be null. Then POST /v1/events with a USD spend.observed for that tenant and confirm 202 with a receipt, not 400.

Control, unchanged behaviour: sqlite3 $DB_PATH "UPDATE tenants SET currency = 'ZZZ' WHERE id = 'tenant_demo'" — /opportunities must still read 'value ₹1,000.00' (the INR fallback), must not render the string 'ZZZ', and must return HTTP 200. POST a USD spend.observed for that tenant and confirm it is still 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH with tenant_currency 'ZZZ' in the details.
Control, genuine mismatch: set the currency back to 'USD' and POST a spend.observed with currency EUR — still 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH.
npm run sdlc:verify green, and test/web/pages.test.js green with one 'opp_usd_expensive' fixture block and one 'const envelope = (event_id' definition in the file.
evidence: Reproduced on origin/main, unmodified, with a throwaway renderPage harness: tenants.create({currency: 'usd'}) plus a USD spend.observed of 3_000_000_000 and one lead_qualified renders opportunity value 'value ₹6,000.00' (the QA report), Qualified CPL '—' (not in the QA report), and the dashboard insight spend as '₹4,000.00' rather than '$4,000.00'.

The em-dash is the funnel exclusion, not the money fallback: computeFunnel(events, 'usd') skips every spend.observed whose payload.currency is 'USD' (src/domain/measurement.js:203), leaving spend_micros 0, so qualified_cpl_micros is null by the zero-spend rule. The identical path at src/api/routes.js:170 makes GET /v1/metrics report the same zero.
The same string comparison at src/api/routes.js:146 rejects a USD spend.observed for a 'usd' tenant as CURRENCY_MISMATCH, because 'USD' !== 'usd'.
ISO_CURRENCIES.includes is false for 'usd', 'Usd' and ' USD ' (checked directly against src/domain/money.js on main), so every one of those misses the guard at src/web/pages.js:216.

Nothing the app writes produces such a row: src/domain/measurement.js:124 and :136 validate ingest currency with the same exact ISO_CURRENCIES.includes, and src/api/routes.js:158 seeds a new tenant's currency from that validated code. The non-canonical row comes from outside the write path — a human UPDATE, as in the QA repro, or a legacy import.

Review finding 1 confirmed on main: test/web/pages.test.js:1017-1021 is the guard, and it filters on event_type === 'lead_qualified' and asserts a count of 1; no assertion anywhere before the render loop touches the spend.observed payload's amount_micros.

Review finding 2 confirmed on main: diff of test/web/pages.test.js lines 931-941 against 978-988 is empty, and the `envelope` closure at 1001-1006 differs from the ones at 295-300 and 339-344 by exactly one line, the tenant_id literal.
risks: money() is the last line before a number reaches a reader, so its fallback now depends on canonicalCurrency. A code that resolves to a real ISO currency but whose MINOR_EXPONENTS entry is missing (a 0- or 3-digit currency such as JPY or BHD) now renders where it previously fell back to INR. That is the correct unit, and microsPerMinorUnit already defaults to 2 for those, so the split maths is unchanged — but it is a real behaviour change for any tenant whose code is a valid non-2-exponent currency written in lower case, and it is the intended fix.

Relaxing the ingest mismatch check means a 'usd' tenant now accepts USD spend it used to reject. That is the point, but it is the one place where this order makes the write path more permissive, so the genuine-mismatch control in the tests and in qa_script step 7 matters: 'USD' tenant + EUR spend must still 400.

The CURRENCY_MISMATCH error's message and details keep the stored string verbatim, so an operator with a 'usd' row who now gets a 202 will see no message at all; the canonicalisation is silent by design. Accepted: the row is bad data, the numbers are right, and no in-app write path produces the row.

The test-file refactor touches two existing USD tests that the #44 work order fenced off. The fence is lifted by this order, deliberately, at the reviewer's own suggestion, so a reviewer who does not know that will read the diff as a constraint violation. The change must be a pure move: no assertion in either test may change.

usdRepos() returning a repos object with tenant and opportunity pre-seeded means a caller that also needs events or an experiment mutates it further. If an implementer instead threads options through the helper, the call sites stop being one-liners and the indirection cost returns.
out_of_scope: Rejecting a non-canonical code on write (tenants.create throwing or coercing). The issue offers it as the alternative, and it is the weaker of the two here: the QA repro sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE, which never reaches tenants.create, so a write-side guard would not fix the reported case and would break the deliberate 'accepts any string, render must not 500' contract pinned at test/web/pages.test.js:1077.

Repairing existing non-canonical tenant rows in storage — a migration or a seed-time normalisation. Nothing in the app writes such rows today (see evidence), the read-side fix makes them render correctly wherever they exist, and a data migration on a table a human can edit is a separate decision with its own rollback story.
The Meta error-shell test at test/web/pages.test.js:1059, which needs a tenant and no opportunity. It keeps its own single-line tenants.create; do not widen usdRepos() to serve it.
The two mixed-currency tenant_demo tests' fixtures beyond their envelope closures. They share validatedEnvelope() and nothing else.

Any change to assertValidCurrency, fromMicros or the INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour in src/domain/money.js. canonicalCurrency is a read-time boundary, not a second constructor, and loosening the constructor is a separate decision about the money contract.

Splitting the ticket. Findings 1 and 2 are the same file and the same test, and finding 3 is the defect that test guards; the reviewer explicitly asked for the fixture lift to be owned by whoever writes the order. Planning them together is cheaper than three trips through the council, and the ticket says to split only if they turn out to be unrelated.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim here was executed against main rather than read off the report: the three findings reproduce, and the currency defect reproduces with a worse symptom than was filed (the em-dash CPL, found by running it rather than by reasoning about the report). The change is a one-function addition plus two mechanical read-site replacements and one comparison, with no new dependency and no schema change, and the existing suite pins the behaviour on both sides of it — the 'ZZZ' fallback test and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH test are the safety net for the permissive direction. The 12 points held back are the DRY refactor: it touches two tests this ticket's own predecessor fenced off, it is a pure move across ~90 lines, and it is the kind of change that can quietly alter a fixture. The implementer must run the file before and after, not just after.

alternatives_considered.approach: Canonicalise in tenants.create on write, coercing the stored row to its canonical form.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not fix the reported repro, which sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE and never reaches the repository. It would also break the contract test/web/pages.test.js:1077 pins — that tenants.create accepts any string and a page render must not 500 on bad data — and it would silently rewrite operator-supplied data. Read-side canonicalisation covers every source of a bad row, which is a superset of what write-side covers.

alternatives_considered.approach: Reject the non-canonical code at the render boundary: keep the INR fallback but return an error panel or an unformatted 'USD 6,000.00' when the stored code is merely mis-cased.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The money() doc comment already argues the opposite trade deliberately — a correctly-formatted amount in the repo default over a mislabelled-but-honest one. And the honest-label option does not help here: 'usd' is not bad data in the way 'ZZZ' is, it is the same currency with different typing, and a reader seeing 'USD 6,000.00' instead of '$6,000.00' learns nothing was wrong.

alternatives_considered.approach: Loosen assertValidCurrency in money.js so fromMicros itself accepts and normalises 'usd', and let the three comparison sites stay as they are.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes the money constructor's contract rather than its consumers, so the INVALID_CURRENCY behaviour test/domain/money.test.js already pins moves for every caller, and it still does not fix computeFunnel's tenant-currency comparison, which is a string compare with no money constructor in it. The defect is at the read boundary, so that is where the fix belongs.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the currency defect in this ticket and file findings 1 and 2 as a separate cleanup issue.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ticket bundles them on purpose and the reviewer's own note on finding 2 asks for the fixture lift to be owned by whoever holds the order. All three land in test/web/pages.test.js plus the currency path that file guards, and the new canonicalisation test wants the very helper findings 1 and 2 ask for. Splitting would mean the helper lands in one PR and the test that uses it in another.

assumptions: Trim-and-upper is the right canonicalisation for ISO 4217 codes, and no tenant needs a code that is legitimately mixed-case or padded. ISO 4217 codes are upper-case alpha-3 by definition, so the mapping is total on well-formed input and a no-op on canonical input.

A mis-cased or padded tenant code is bad data, not a distinct unit of account, and no tenant row anywhere in the wild holds a code that canonicalises to something other than what was meant. The only sources are a human UPDATE and a legacy import; the app's own write path already emits canonical codes.
unknowns: Whether any deployed database outside this repo holds a non-canonical tenant row. Nothing in the repo enumerates tenants beyond the demo one, and the read-side fix makes such a row render correctly whether or not it exists, so the answer does not change the work — it changes only whether QA ever sees the bug in the wild.

Whether a tenant row could ever legitimately hold a currency outside ISO_CURRENCIES that this build should still render. The 'ZZZ' test says no: unknown is bad data and INR is the documented fallback. This ticket does not revisit that decision.
residual_risks: A stored code that is mis-cased AND a currency with no 2-digit minor unit now renders in its own unit for the first time, where before it drew rupees. If any such row exists, the numbers a reader sees will change currency on upgrade. That is the fix, not a regression, and no test asserts the old value for such a row — but QA should read the first AC-1 render as a deliberate change rather than a diff to be accepted at a glance.

A non-canonical row stays non-canonical in storage after this change. It renders correctly everywhere now, but the next reader of the tenants table sees 'usd' and may reasonably assume the app normalises on write. It does not. The fix is stated at the read boundary in the money() doc comment, which is the only place a future implementer is likely to be looking.
